svg.title: Amazon Route 53
svg.desc: Amazon Route 53. Managed DNS: hosted zones, routing policies (weighted, latency, failover, geolocation) and health checks. Step 1, Where it sits: Every visit starts with a lookup: the site goes to CloudFront, the API to the closest healthy ALB. Step 2, One lookup, end to end: A cold resolver walks root → .example → Route 53, which answers with Thailand's ALB for 60 s. Step 3, Health checks and failover: api-th fails /health 3 times: Route 53 drops it, new lookups get Singapore, status goes to S3. Step 4, Limits and costs: Failover waits for 3 checks plus the TTL; checkers can't reach private IPs; weights split lookups.

g.text: Every visit starts with a lookup: the site goes to CloudFront, the API to the closest healthy ALB.
A cold resolver walks root → .example → Route 53, which answers with Thailand's ALB for 60 s.
api-th fails /health 3 times: Route 53 drops it, new lookups get Singapore, status goes to S3.
Failover waits for 3 checks plus the TTL; checkers can't reach private IPs; weights split lookups.
then HTTPS to the address in the answer
$0.40 per million queries · alias to AWS: free
answers only inside the VPCs it is associated with
serves the site from the edge
THE FIRST HOP OF EVERY VISIT
Before any request reaches Acme Shop, the phone’s resolver asks one of the zone’s four Route 53 name servers where a name points.
The site at the zone apex goes to CloudFront and the API to the closest healthy load balancer: Thailand’s for a user in Chiang Mai.
Inside the VPC, the private zone acme.internal turns db.acme.internal into the RDS endpoint; outside it, that name doesn’t resolve.
A COLD CACHE WALKS THE DELEGATION
The root names the .example servers, and they name the zone’s four
Route 53 servers, which resolvers keep for about two days. Route 53
takes the weight-90 branch, then the Region with the lowest latency.
An alias answers with the target’s current IPs as an A record. It
works at the zone apex, where a CNAME can’t; queries to AWS targets
are free; the TTL is the target’s: 60 s for a load balancer.
Checkers in 8 Regions probe every 30 s. Each must connect within 4 s
and get a 2xx or 3xx within 2 s; 3 misses in a row count as down.
At 18% healthy or less, Route 53 marks api-th unhealthy.
stable.api skips api-th: the next-lowest latency is Singapore. status
fails over to the S3 page, and 10% of api lookups still reach the
canary. Resolvers keep the old answer until its 60 s TTL runs out.
HOW LONG A FAILOVER TAKES HERE
plus any resolver or app that keeps answers longer than told
Checkers can’t reach private IPs: alarm on a CloudWatch metric instead.
Weights split lookups, not requests: one cached answer serves many users.
Flip Regions on command with ARC routing controls; sign the zone with DNSSEC.
